jobs.title: Tenure-Track Faculty in NanoEngineering for 2027-2028
jobs.description:
The Department of Physics, Optical Engineering, and NanoEngineering (PHON) at Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology seeks applicants for a tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant Professor level to support the NanoEngineering degree program starting August 2027. Candidates with advanced experience may be considered for appointment at a higher academic rank. Our teaching-focused mission is “to provide students with the world’s best undergraduate science, engineering, and mathematics education in an environment of individual attention and support.” If this resonates with you, then we think you’ll love what we have to offer.
The candidate we hire will join a team of 21 members dedicated to delivering undergraduate major programs in physics, nanoengineering, and optical engineering, as well as an M.S. program in optical engineering. The department also supports several minors and certificates, including a semiconductor certificate, an astronomy minor, a quantum information certificate, and a nanoengineering minor. Active research programs related to NanoEngineering include semiconductors, nanotechnology, light matter interactions, and quantum materials. In addition, NanoEngineering houses the primary users of a cleanroom (MiNDS Facility) for undergraduate teaching and research in nanotechnology, with resources including e-beam lithography, atomic layer deposition, nanoimprint lithography, and other standard cleanroom tools. Undergraduate courses in the areas of semiconductor devices, nanotechnology, and MEMS are taught in the cleanroom. Additional information on Rose-Hulman and the Physics, Optical Engineering, and NanoEngineering Department is available from https://www.rose-hulman.edu/PHON.
Essential job responsibilities include teaching and mentoring students, continued professional development, and service to the department, Institute, and professional community. The successful candidate will use effective approaches to teach introductory physics courses and labs, as well as upper division courses in nanoengineering, including lab courses in the cleanroom. The candidate will have the opportunity to develop and teach upper-level electives in their area of expertise. Please visit our course catalog at https://catalog.rose-hulman.edu/catalog/ for descriptions of our existing courses. Research and scholarship remain an integral part of the role — professional development at Rose-Hulman is defined broadly as continued intellectual growth throughout one's career, which may include scholarship of discovery, integration, application, teaching, or learning, often carried out in partnership with undergraduate students — but it supports the teaching mission rather than competing with it. Service expectations within the department include advising students, curriculum development and continuous improvement, and participation in departmental activities.
Requirements include a Ph.D. degree in engineering by the time of appointment and evidence of, or demonstrated potential for, excellence in undergraduate teaching. Prior cleanroom or nanofabrication experience is essential and a degree focusing on semiconductors, microfabrication, nanotechnology, or materials engineering is preferred. Candidates with prior teaching, relevant industry, or postdoc experience are also preferred. The department and institute place a high value on supporting all our students; candidates who are excited to enhance student engagement and community are especially encouraged to apply.
Review of applications will start December 16, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled. Interested candidates should submit a curriculum vitae, a cover letter that summarizes teaching and research objectives at a primarily undergraduate institution, a 1-2 page teaching philosophy that includes evidence of, or potential for, teaching effectiveness and a plan for continued growth in teaching, a 1-2 page statement of professional development/research objectives involving undergraduate students, and a list of 3 references who can speak to your teaching and mentoring abilities. Please apply online at https://jobs.rose-hulman.edu.
Rose-Hulman is one of the nation’s top undergraduate engineering, science, and mathematics colleges and is home to 2,100 students with a passion for STEM and learning. See what the media and our peer institutions have said by visiting https://www.rose-hulman.edu/about-us/rankings-and-distinction.html.
Contact person: Dr. Galen Duree, Department Head, Department of Physics, Optical Engineering, and NanoEngineering, Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology, 5500 Wabash Avenue CM 169, Terre Haute, IN 47803 or emailed to duree@rose-hulman.edu.
Applications: Only online applications/resumes submitted via the Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology Employment Opportunities website, jobs.rose-hulman.edu, will be considered. For application system questions or assistance, please contact Human Resources via email, HRApply@rose-hulman.edu.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Assistant or Associate Professor of Wildlife Care and
Rehabilitation (Remote)
Description
Husson Universitys School of Online and Professional Studies
invites applications for a full-time Assistant or Associate
Professor of Wildlife Care and Rehabilitation. The ideal candidate
will have the academic background and experience to help lead
Hussons new online Bachelors degree in Wildlife Care and
Rehabilitation. The successful candidate will have a history of
scholarship in wildlife care and rehabilitation, wildlife medicine,
wildlife anatomy and physiology, human dimensions of wildlife care
and rehabilitation, animal behavior, or animal welfare. The
successful candidate will be expected to teach online bachelors-
and masters-level courses in Wildlife Care and Management;
Designing Captive Wildlife Experiences; Wildlife Rescue, Transport,
and Triage; Human Dimensions of Wildlife Care and Rehabilitation;
and Animal Welfare, along with other topics within the specific
area of expertise. This is a fully remote, 12 month position, with
expectations of online teaching plus other disciplinary and
departmental responsibilities. Applicants must be U.S.
citizens.
Husson University is a private Doctoral/Professional institution
located in Bangor, Maine. The University is dedicated to offering
premier professional programs designed to maximize experiential
learning opportunities and student success. Husson University
prides itself on providing first-class online professional
education that is based in rigor and engaging learning.
Example of Duties
The primary responsibilities of this position include teaching
online courses for undergraduate students in the online Bachelors
of Wildlife Care and Rehabilitation major as well as undergraduate
or graduate courses in related programs. The successful candidate
will also fulfill faculty expectations for participation in
departmental service such as oversight and assessment of these
growing programs and the development of online courses. The
position requires teaching 24 credits of online courses per
academic year and additional course development and curriculum
duties as assigned. Faculty also are expected to excel in
scholarship and service.
Essential Functions:
Instruct undergraduate and graduate online wildlife care and
rehabilitation courses, plus other courses as assigned, using the
MLS system Canvas.
Develop online undergraduate and graduate wildlife care and
rehabilitation courses.
Implement appropriate pedagogical techniques for the online
environment, including facilitating student engagement and
providing student feedback and support.
Support assessment of online courses and curricula.
Engage in research and scholarly work appropriate for the
faculty rank.
Participate in admissions events as assigned and support
recruitment.
Professionally represent Husson University in all university
activities, including teaching, scholarship, and outreach.
Guide capstone projects in assigned programs as needed.
Participate in faculty governance as assigned.
Support students with networking and career development.
Qualifications
Requirements for the position include an earned doctoral degree
with a focus in wildlife care and rehabilitation or a related
field; ABD considered. The successful candidate will demonstrate
commitment to effective online teaching and student learning, and
possess strong communication skills. Preference will be given to
applications with previous higher education online teaching
experience and evidence of scholarly activities.
Supplemental Information
The physical demands described here are representative of those
that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the
functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to
enable individuals with disabilities to perform their
functions.
Effectively communicate with students and colleagues
Read and interpret with vision ability for close and distance
vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
Sit or stand for extended periods of time.
Bend, kneel, and reach with the use of hands and arms.
Utilize telephone, email, and other approved communications
systems.
Operate a computer, printer, webcam, manage multiple monitors
and switch between multiple computer applications as needed.
Works from a home office with reliable internet, a computer,
webcam, and headset.
Uses learning management systems to deliver course materials,
communicate with students, and manage grades.
May teach live virtual classes, asynchronous courses, or a mix
of both.
Review of applicants will continue until the position is filled.
A complete application must include a cover letter, curriculum
vitae, a statement of teaching philosophy, and contact information
for three references (at least one must be able to discuss online
teaching potential).

Cover letter

Job Description
The United Arab Emirates University invites applications for a faculty position at the Assistant Professor level in Experimental High Energy Physics. We seek an outstanding candidate with a strong research background and active participation in large-scale international collaborations such as the ATLAS experiment at CERN. Priority will be given to candidates with demonstrated expertise in the ATLAS Tile Calorimeter, including its operation, performance, calibration, and involvement in Phase-II upgrades and future detector developments for the High-Luminosity LHC. Experience in detector instrumentation and hardware–software integration is highly desirable. In addition, strong expertise in computing is highly valued, particularly in high-performance and distributed computing environments such as the Worldwide LHC Computing Grid (WLCG), as well as in data-intensive analysis and modern approaches including machine learning and artificial intelligence applications in particle physics. The candidate is also expected to participate in the department’s administrative services as well as community activities. The successful candidate will benefit from a competitive tax-free salary package, including free accommodation, health insurance, children’s education support, relocation and furniture allowances, and annual airfare tickets. Applicants must submit all required materials through the UAEU recruitment portal at https://jobs.uaeu.ac.ae, noting that incomplete applications will not be considered.

Candidates must hold a PhD in Experimental High Energy Physics, preferably with experience in large international collaborations such as CERN’s ATLAS experiment, especially the Tile Calorimeter. Strong skills in computing, data analysis, and modern techniques like machine learning are highly desirable. Applicants should have completed ATLAS qualification tasks and hold full membership to begin work immediately. Teaching experience and top journals publications are preferred.

PhD in Experimental High Energy Physics (preferably with experience in large-scale international collaborations such as CERN’s ATLAS experiment). Applicants should have completed ATLAS qualification tasks and hold full membership to begin work immediately.

Assistant Professor

Job Details
Position Title: Endowed Bartlett Chair Professor/Associate
Professor, Free Enterprise

Location: Waltham, MA
Description:
Job Description Summary
Bentley University invites applications for the Bartlett Chair
of Free Enterprise, an endowed position at the Associate or Full
Professor level, to begin in Fall 2027.
Funded by a generous gift from Bruce and Patricia Bartlett, the
Bartlett Chair of Free Enterprise affirms Bentley's commitment to
fostering free expression, intellectual pluralism, and the
constructive exchange of ideas as central to a liberal education.
Free Enterprise encompasses the institutions and conditions that
enable individuals and organizations to pursue entrepreneurial
ideas, enter and compete in markets, and create economic and
societal value, while examining the legal, ethical, technological,
and regulatory frameworks necessary to ensure fair competition and
meaningful participation.
This position is part of a broader Bartlett initiative that also
includes a companion Chair of Free Speech. The two chairs will work
together to build programming, events, and curricular initiatives
under the Bartlett banner that promote inquiry, debate, and
engagement across disciplines.
The Bartlett Chair of Free Enterprise carries a 1-1 teaching
load, providing substantial support for research, public
engagement, and leadership of the Bartlett initiative. This support
includes summer salary, a chair stipend, and a generous research
and travel account.
Qualifications
A Ph.D. in a related business, economics, technology, law or
policy related field is required.
The successful candidate will demonstrate:
A distinguished record of research, teaching, and public
engagement appropriate to appointment at the Associate or Full
Professor level.
An active and high-quality research agenda that reflects a
robust commitment to the principles of free enterprise.
Strength in interdisciplinary teaching and dialogue across
fields.
We especially welcome candidates whose work engages some of the
following potential areas of focus:
Entrepreneurship, new venture creation, and barriers to market
entry
Historical, ethical, and legal considerations in free enterprise
and market/capitalist economies
Competition, market concentration, and antitrust
Regulation and its effects on innovation and business
formation
The role of digital technologies, such as A.I., in shaping
market participation, innovation, competition, and entrepreneurial
opportunity
Candidates with experience in public-facing scholarship, civic
dialogue, media engagement, or leading campus and community
conversations are particularly encouraged to apply.
Responsibilities
Teaching
Teach one course per semester, reflecting a 1-1 teaching
load.
Offer undergraduate courses on free enterprise, free markets,
and related topics.
Develop a Free Enterprise course within the Falcon Discovery
Seminar (first-year program).
Foster rigorous, inclusive, and intellectually open classroom
environments in which students can engage constructively with
competing ideas and perspectives.
Scholarship
Maintain an active and visible research agenda related to free
enterprise, or closely connected areas of inquiry.
Publish in scholarly journals and public-facing venues.
Present research and ideas at national and international
conferences, public forums, and professional gatherings.
Contribute to public conversations about free enterprise through
writing, speaking, media engagement, or related activities.
Develop and sustain relationships with relevant scholarly,
professional, and civic organizations (e.g., American Enterprise
Institute, Heritage Foundation, or Cato Institute).
Campus Engagement and the Bartlett Initiative
Collaborate closely with the Bartlett Chair of Free Speech on
joint programming, including speaker series, public events, and
curricular initiatives.
Help shape and advance a compelling long-term vision for the
Bartlett initiative.
Lead campus conversations on the role of free enterprise and its
place in society.
Working with the Dean of Arts & Sciences and the Dean of
Business, the Bartlett Chairs will jointly shape a visible and
intellectually vibrant set of initiatives that connect free speech
and free enterprise as foundations of liberal education.
Bentley is committed to the teacher-scholar model, where
teaching, scholarship, service, and community engagement are
valued. Bentley values intellectual diversity alongside diversity
of background and experience and seeks faculty who can contribute
to a culture of open inquiry, free expression, mutual respect, and
constructive engagement across differences in viewpoint.
Bentley University, located in suburban Boston, is an AACSB and
NECHE accredited institution that enrolls approximately 5,200
students at the undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral levels.
Bentley is ranked at or near the top in several categories by US
News & World Report, including Best Regional Universities North
and Most Innovative Schools, with Bloomberg ranking Bentley in the
top 20 undergraduate business programs. Bentley's high graduation
and retention rates and top-ranked Pulsifer Career Center reflects
a commitment to student success and inclusiveness. With a strong
faculty of teacher-scholars, Bentley strives to be a "Force for
Good" through the integration of business with the arts and
sciences, and a strong emphasis on ethics and social
responsibility. Providing a stimulating academic community for
faculty, staff, and students, Bentley supports its faculty as they
pursue cutting-edge research and bring their expertise and real
world understanding into the classroom.
Application Materials
Applicants should submit:
An up-to-date curriculum vitae.
A letter of interest that:
Describes their qualifications for the Bartlett Chair of Free
Enterprise
Explains the direct and substantive relationship of the
candidate's scholarship, teaching, public engagement, and
professional activities to the themes of free enterprise.
Outlines the candidates vision or ideas for advancing the
Bartlett initiative through programming, teaching, scholarship,
external engagement, and campus dialogue.
A teaching statement that includes a description of how the
candidate has demonstrated, or intends to create and support, an
inclusive classroom environment.
A teaching portfolio including sample syllabi and available
student and/or peer evaluations.
A brief research statement, along with up to five scholarly
works that the candidate wishes the committee to emphasize when
evaluating their research and scholarship in the area of free
enterprise.
The names and contact information of three references. Bentley
will contact these individuals confidentially only for candidates
who advance in the search process.
Application Deadline: For full consideration,
applications should be submitted by November 1, 2026. Candidate
reviews will continue until the position is filled.
Pay Transparency
At Bentley we offer a "total rewards" package designed to
attract, motivate, retain, and reward our employees. This includes
competitive compensation, robust benefits, career development and
opportunities, generous paid time off, workplace flexibility and a
positive, engaging employee experience. In alignment with the
Massachusetts Pay Transparency Act and our commitment to equity and
transparency, we're sharing the salary grade range for this role.
The grade range is based on market data and the scope of
responsibilities. Final pay will depend on your experience,
education, home department, and other relevant qualifications.
Professor Rank Range: $160,000 - $260,000
Associate Professor Rank Range: $140,000 - $235,000
If you have questions about the salary grade range or need
additional information, please contact us at
GA_HR_Employment@bentley.edu.

Bentley University strives to create a campus community that

community.

ABOUT US
QUALIFICATIONS
Program Description
The Leveraging Excellence Across Disciplines (LEAD) Faculty
Fellowship is a professional development program designed to
prepare a broad and talented pool of educators equipped to teach
and support the increasingly diverse community college student
population. The program is open to all individuals interested in
developing their teaching experience in the community college
setting. A collaborative initiative between the Office of
Diversity, Equity and Inclusion and the Office of the Provost, the
fellowship provides compensated teaching experience, structured
mentorship, and professional development to prepare participants
for future full-time faculty roles.
The LEAD Faculty Fellowship aligns with Harper College’s commitment
to academic excellence, inclusive teaching practices, and student
success. Fellows receive a paid appointment of up to two years
beginning each fall; continuation into the second year is
contingent upon satisfactory performance and the Dean’s approval.
If hired into a full-time role, the second year may apply toward
tenure.
This fellowship will begin in August 2026.
Eligibility
Applicants must meet the departmental faculty credentials
statement. Credentials vary by discipline and may require a
master’s degree or a master’s or bachelor’s degree combined with
relevant professional experience. For specific departmental
credentials, please contact Human Resources at
hr@harpercollege.edu. Applicants must also have fewer than three
years of full-time teaching experience as the instructor of
record.
The College is particularly interested in applicants eligible to
teach in Economics, English, Political Science, Geography, Health
Science Core, and Mathematics; however, applicants from all
disciplines are encouraged to apply.
Responsibilities
LEAD Faculty Fellows will have a reduced teaching load during the
first year and, if approved to continue in the fellowship, will
move toward a full teaching load in the second year. Fellows will
observe and shadow senior faculty members, participate in ongoing
goal setting and feedback sessions with mentors, engage in shared
governance activities, interact with faculty and staff across
campus, and participate in a range of professional development
opportunities.
Duties & Responsibilities
Teach assigned credit hours each academic year
Design inclusive course content and syllabi
Maintain office hours
Engage regularly with designated mentors
Attend monthly professional development sessions
Attend internal and external professional development
opportunities
Set professional goals and priorities annually
Build strong, supportive relationships with students, faculty,
and staff
Observe and shadow senior faculty members
Participate in ongoing feedback and performance
evaluations
Utilize institutional resources to strengthen instructional
capacity
Participate in selected shared governance committee
meetings
Attend Faculty Senate and division/department meetings
Develop and maintain a digital professional portfolio
Participate in an Employee Resource Group
Attend programs sponsored by the Office of Diversity, Equity
and Inclusion
Reporting & Evaluation
LEAD Faculty Fellows will report to and be evaluated by their
Division Dean. The Vice President for Diversity, Equity and
Inclusion will convene regular “Success Team Meetings” with
Fellows, their Division Dean, and designated mentors. Monthly
professional development lunches are required.
Application Process
Applications must be completed online and include the following
materials:
Letter of interest (two pages maximum)
Current vita or resume
Unofficial transcripts
Contact information for three professional references
Official transcripts are required prior to Board of Trustees
approval. Employment is contingent upon a criminal background
check. Employment sponsorship is not available.
Application Deadline
Candidates who submit complete application materials by January 5,
2026, will receive full consideration.

jobs.title: Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor - Basic and Translational Vision Science  - (497323 )
jobs.description:
Job Details
Department: Vision
SciencesSalary: Commensurate with experience
Description:
The University of Houston's College of Optometry invites
applications for an open-rank, tenure-track or tenured, faculty
position in the Department of Vision Sciences. We seek an
outstanding scientist to establish or maintain a nationally
recognized, independent, externally funded research program
addressing fundamental biological mechanisms of eye and visual
system development, function, and disease.
We are particularly interested in investigators whose research
complements and expands the College's strengths in ocular growth
and development, myopia, ocular biology, biomedical imaging, and
translational clinical research. Candidates may employ molecular,
cellular, physiological, behavioral, imaging, computational, or
other innovative experimental approaches.
The successful candidate will join a collaborative research
environment that connects fundamental scientific discovery with
clinical investigation and opportunities to improve the prevention,
diagnosis, and treatment of eye disease.
Areas of Research Interest
All areas of basic and translational vision science will be
considered, with particular interest in the following:
Ocular Growth, Development, and Myopia
• Biological, physiological, genetic, and environmental mechanisms
regulating ocular growth and refractive development.
• Experimental investigations of myopia development, progression,
and potential therapeutic interventions.
Ocular Metabolism, Nutrition, and Precision Vision Health
• Metabolic and nutritional influences on ocular development,
visual function, aging, and disease.
• Molecular and cellular mechanisms linking systemic health with
ocular tissue biology and opportunities for precision medicine.
Pre-clinical Models of Ocular Disease
• Development and application of animal models to investigate
normal visual function and disease mechanisms.
• Comparative and translational investigations involving
experimental models, including marmosets and rhesus macaques.
Ocular Pharmacology and Therapeutic Discovery
• Molecular and cellular mechanisms of ocular disease and
therapeutic response.
• Drug discovery, identification of novel therapeutic targets, and
experimental approaches to disease prevention and treatment.
These areas are illustrative rather than restrictive. Candidates
with compelling research programs that introduce complementary
expertise or innovative methodologies are encouraged to apply.
Research Environment:
The University of Houston College of Optometry offers a
productive and well-supported research environment spanning basic
biological investigations, experimental models, biomedical imaging,
and clinical research.
Research resources and opportunities include:
• An established community of basic and clinical vision scientists
engaged in collaborative, nationally recognized research.
• A National Eye Institute-supported P30 core grant providing
shared resources in instrumentation and optical design,
programming, biostatistics, histology, and biomedical
imaging.
• Experimental capabilities involving cellular and tissue systems,
animal models, including nonhuman primates, advanced imaging, and
physiological and behavioral methods.
• Access to a large clinical population supporting patient-based
and translational research.
• A developing cloud-based health data infrastructure supporting
the integration and analysis of biological, clinical, imaging, and
computational datasets.
• Opportunities for collaboration across the University of Houston
and with biomedical investigators in the neighboring Texas Medical
Center.
Faculty Responsibilities:
The successful candidate will be expected to:
• Develop and sustain an independent, nationally recognized
research program supported by competitive external funding,
particularly from the National Institutes of Health.
• Publish significant original research and contribute to
collaborative scientific initiatives.
• Teach in the College's graduate and Doctor of Optometry
professional programs in areas aligned with the candidate's
expertise.
• Mentor graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, and professional
students engaged in biomedical research.
• Participate in academic service and contribute to the College's
research and educational missions.
Qualifications:
Required Qualifications
• An earned Ph.D., O.D./Ph.D., M.D., or equivalent doctoral degree
in vision science, neuroscience, biomedical engineering, biology,
physiology, pharmacology, or a related biomedical discipline.
• Demonstrated research expertise relevant to eye and vision
science.
• Evidence of scientific productivity and the potential to
establish or sustain an independent, externally funded research
program.
• Strong communication and collaborative skills, with a commitment
to research mentorship and education.
Preferred Qualifications
• Postdoctoral or equivalent advanced research experience.
• A strong record of peer-reviewed publications and competitive
external funding, appropriate to career stage.
• Research expertise in ocular growth and development, myopia,
ocular metabolism, nutrition, experimental disease models,
pharmacology, or related biomedical sciences.
• Experience with innovative experimental approaches and productive
scientific collaboration.
• Experience teaching and mentoring graduate or professional
students.
Faculty Appointment:
This is an open-rank, tenure-track or tenured, faculty position
in the Department of Vision Sciences. Appointments may be made at
the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor level. Rank, salary,
and start-up support will be competitive and commensurate with
qualifications, experience, and research program requirements.
Application Process
Review of applications will begin upon posting and continue until
the position is filled. For fullest consideration, applications
should be received by February 15, 2027.
Applicants should submit:
1. Cover letter describing their qualifications, research
interests, and potential contributions to the Department of Vision
Sciences.
2. Curriculum vitae.
3. Research statement outlining accomplishments, current
activities, and future directions (2–3 pages).
4. Statement of teaching and mentoring interests (1–2 pages).
5. Names and contact information for three professional
references.
Please contact, Dr. Vallabh Das, Dept. Chair of Vision Sciences at
vdas@Central.UH.EDU or Dr. Geunyoung Yoon, Search
Committee Chair at gyoon2@central.uh.edu should you have any follow-up
questions.
About the University of Houston College of
Optometry:
The University of Houston College of Optometry is
internationally recognized for excellence in professional
optometric education, biomedical vision research, and
evidence-based clinical care. Its research enterprise spans
fundamental biological discovery, experimental investigations, and
clinical and translational studies.
Located in Houston, the College offers exceptional opportunities
for scientific collaboration through its established clinical
programs, the University's interdisciplinary research community,
and proximity to the Texas Medical Center.
Employees are expected to have a home address in the state of
Texas for the duration of their appointments.
Official transcripts are required for a faculty appointment and
will be requested upon selection of the final candidates.
All positions at the University of Houston-System are security
sensitive and will require a criminal history check. Individuals
conducting research in critical infrastructure areas (i.e.,
communication infrastructure systems, cybersecurity systems,
electric grid, hazardous waste treatment systems, and/or water
treatment facilities) are subject to regular review to ensure the
security and integrity of the research is maintained.
The University of Houston System and its universities are Equal
Opportunity Institutions. Everyone is encouraged to apply.

Title
Assistant Professor in Media, Behavior, and Health

Tenure Track

Position Summary
The Media School at Indiana University’s flagship Bloomington
campus is pleased to announce a faculty search for an outstanding
tenure-track colleague whose research and teaching examine the
relationships among media, behavior, and health, to start August 1,
2027.
We welcome applications from scholars working across a broad range
of topics at the intersection of media, health, and well-being.
Areas of interest may include, but are not limited to, media
influences on mental and physical health; health communication and
health behavior; social media and well-being; media representations
of health, illness, and disability; stigma and stereotyping;
cognitive, emotional, and behavioral responses to health-related
media; health misinformation; and the development and evaluation of
media-based interventions designed to improve health and
well-being. We are particularly interested in scholars whose work
helps explain how media environments, messages, and technologies
shape health-related attitudes, psychological processes,
decision-making, and behavioral outcomes.
We welcome a range of theoretical perspectives and methodological
approaches, including experimental, survey, longitudinal,
computational, neuroscientific, qualitative, and mixed-method
approaches. Candidates may study children, adolescents, adults, or
populations across the lifespan.
This position offers substantial opportunities for
interdisciplinary collaboration across Indiana University,
including with faculty in the Media School, the School of Public
Health, the Department of Psychological and Brain Sciences, the
Irsay Institute, and other units engaged in health and behavioral
research. The successful candidate will join a growing community of
scholars examining media, behavior, health, and well-being across
the campus.
The chosen applicant will be expected to maintain a productive and
theoretically significant research program, effectively teach and
mentor undergraduate and graduate students on a standard 2-2
teaching load, and serve the university, profession, and wider
community. Teaching opportunities may include courses in media
psychology, strategic communications, health communication, social
media, research methods, and other areas related to the candidate’s
expertise.
The primary criteria for this search are excellence in research and
teaching related to media, behavior, and health. Evidence of
potential to secure external funding is viewed
favorably. External funding is conceived broadly to include
government, industry, foundation, and other private sources.
About the School
The Media School combines a long-standing tradition of excellence
in journalism, film, gaming, and communications with a commitment
to digital and interactive media. It fosters a multidisciplinary
approach to education and research, equipping students with the
theoretical and practical tools necessary to lead and innovate in
the media landscape of tomorrow. Faculty members are distinguished
for their scholarly contributions and their dedication to teaching,
offering a dynamic environment for engaging with media theory,
production, and design.
The Media School is home to the Center for Documentary Research and
Practice, the Center for International Media Law and Policy
Studies, the Institute for Communication Research, the Michael I.
Arnolt Center for Investigative Journalism, the National Sports
Journalism Center, the Observatory on Social Media, Indiana Public
Media, Cream and Crimson Studios, the KIX Lab, and the Black Film
Center & Archive. The school serves more than 2,300
undergraduate majors in eight degree programs (Journalism, Media,
Game Design, Cinematic Arts, Global Media, Media Advertising,
Public Relations, and Sports Media). It also offers graduate
degrees (M.S. and Ph.D.) to approximately 75 graduate students, of
whom two-thirds are in a doctoral program. Our state-of-the-art
facilities include equipment for television, film and audio
production, game design, and communication research.
University and Community Setting
Nestled in the lively community of Bloomington, our university
campus is renowned for its stunning limestone architecture and
scenic natural landscapes. This setting fosters a culture that
values both the arts and sciences and provides substantial
opportunities for interdisciplinary research and
collaboration.
Bloomington is a vibrant midsize city located within driving
distance of Indianapolis, Chicago, Cincinnati, Columbus, and
Louisville. Our community is small yet welcoming, a home to people
from all over the world. Bloomington features an active arts
community, with several independent music and performance venues
and one of the best university cinemas in the country. Southern
Indiana is also home to beautiful scenery, and residents enjoy
year-round outdoor activities.
Basic Qualifications
ABD applications considered, but Ph.D. in communication, media,
psychology, public health, or a related field must be completed by
the date of appointment.
Demonstrated potential for research productivity in areas
related to media, behavior, and health.
Effective teaching skills adaptable to undergraduate and
graduate learning environments.
Department Contact for Questions
Questions regarding this position or the application process should
be directed to the chair of the search committee, Dr. Nicole
Martins, The Media School, Indiana University, at
nicomart@iu.edu.
Additional Qualifications
Preferred Qualifications
Demonstrated potential for interdisciplinary
collaboration.
Demonstrated potential to secure external funding.
Demonstrated success working with faculty and student
populations from a wide variety of backgrounds and
experiences.

Binghamton University is a premier public R1 research institution
in the State University of New York (SUNY) system that unites more
than 130 broadly interdisciplinary educational programs with some
of the most vibrant research in the nation. Our unique character -
shaped by our mission, outstanding academics, facilities, and
community life - promotes extraordinary student success, research,
and service; Binghamton University is where our students, faculty
and staff thrive.
Working at Binghamton University is more than about having a great
job - it is about having the opportunity to flourish in an
exciting, engaging environment. Our faculty and staff appreciate
Binghamton's collegial and inclusive culture and its commitment to
excellence, education, innovation, and civic engagement. Our
diverse campus community contributes to our success.
Binghamton merges rigorous academics, distinguished faculty who
value cutting-edge, and community-engaged research, teaching and
service, exceptional staff, and ultramodern facilities to engage
and challenge its 18,000+ students. Our high-achieving student body
represents diverse experiences from first-generation college-goers
to international students. Beyond their talent, these classmates
share a desire to shape the future through technology, insight,
intellectual exploration, and community service.
Job Description:
Research Assistant Professor, Source Project; 10 mo. 3-year term
(renewable)
We seek applicants with a Ph.D. in a Humanities or Social Science
discipline (or from an interdisciplinary doctoral program) who have
a commitment to interdisciplinary and experiential learning to join
the Source Project , Binghamton University's
distinctive first-year research program in the Humanities and
Social Sciences. The position begins September 1, 2027. PhD in hand
by time of appointment required.
The Source Project is a sequence of two, four-credit courses over
the fall and spring semesters (research streams), where first-year
students have the opportunity to conduct authentic research and
generate new results. Students will ask questions and seek answers,
guided by faculty who can help identify topics and appropriate
research methods. Students will produce original projects that
express their findings and learn how to communicate the relevance
of what they have found with classmates as well as others in the
University's Research Days poster sessions.
The successful candidate will teach two research streams per year,
either two sections of one theme or two differently themed streams.
Each stream is capped at 25 students. This amounts to a 2/2
teaching load with a maximum of 50 students each semester. Each
course carries associated departmental rubrics and general
education designations. In addition, the Research Assistant
Professor will be responsible for advising students, a dynamic
research agenda, and University service on behalf of the Source
Project, the External Scholarships and Undergraduate Research
center, and the Division of Academic Affairs.

The University of Hong Kong
Founded in 1911, the University of Hong Kong has attained its
pre-eminence as a research-led comprehensive university through
upholding the highest international standards of excellence in its
research pursuits, scholarship, teaching and learning, and service
to the community. The University is consistently ranked amongst the
world’s top universities: 11th in the QS World University Rankings
2027, 1st in the QS Asia University Rankings 2027, and 33rd in the
Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2027. More
information about HKU can be found at https://hku.hk/ .
The Faculty of Social Sciences, HKU
The Faculty of Social Sciences of The University of Hong Kong was
established in 1967 and has undergone rapid expansion and
significant transformation since then. It comprises five
Departments, two Schools, eight research centres and one research
Hub. The Faculty aims to contribute to the advancement of society
and the development of leaders locally, regionally, and globally,
seeking to make a positive social contribution through a global
presence, regional significance and engagement with the rest of
China. The Faculty delivers impact through internationalisation,
innovation and interdisciplinarity. It attracts and nurtures global
scholars through excellence in research, teaching and learning and
knowledge exchange.
The Faculty has been a major research hub in the region and was
ranked 5th in Asia and 22nd in the world in 2026 according to the
QS World University Ranking. Among the five departments, two ranked
top 3 in Asia and three ranked top 25 in the world. Our ongoing
success propels us toward our goal of becoming the foremost social
sciences institution in Asia. More information about the Faculty
can be found at https://www.socsc.hku.hk .
The Position
The Faculty is seeking an outstanding scholar with proven
international leadership in research, teaching and knowledge
exchange in the field of computational social science. Applications
are invited for appointment as Professor/ Associate Professor/
Assistant Professor within the Faculty of Social Sciences, with a
start date of September 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.
Exceptionally outstanding candidates at Professor/ Associate
Professor levels may be considered for appointment on direct tenure
terms subject to the University’s approval.
Applicants should possess a Ph.D. degree in social sciences or
related fields with a focus on computational social science, social
implications of AI, and dynamics of social systems. Ideal
candidates will bring deep expertise in developing and applying
advanced computational and quantitative methodologies—including
artificial intelligence, machine learning, and big data
analytics—to complex social questions. We are looking for
collaborative leaders with a demonstrated ability to bridge
disciplines, driving empirical analyses at the intersection of AI,
technology, and social dynamics. The appointee should have a strong
research track record with publications in leading academic
journals. The appointee will also be responsible for teaching
courses and supervising students at both graduate and undergraduate
levels, directing the undergraduate major in Computational Social
Science, and contributing to the administration of academic
programmes.
What We Offer
A competitive remuneration package commensurate with qualifications
and experience will be offered, in addition to annual leave and
medical benefits. At current rates, salaries tax does not exceed
15% of gross income. The appointment will attract a contract-end
gratuity and University contribution to a retirement benefits
scheme, totalling up to 15% of basic salary. Housing benefits will
be provided as applicable.
Nominations and Applications
HKU has retained Perrett Laver Ltd, an executive search firm, to
assist with the search. All inquiries, nominations/referrals, and
applications (including resume and letter of interest responding to
the requirements outlined in the position profile) should be
directed in confidence to Mr. Matthew Foreman at matthew.foreman@perrettlaver.com
.
Review of nominations and applications will continue until
January 31, 2027 , or until the post is filled, whichever is
earlier.
Advertised: Nov 16, 2026 (HK Time)
Applications close: Jan 31, 2027 (HK Time)

jobs.title: Teaching Assistant Professor - ICOM
jobs.description:
The College of Information and Communications (CIC) at the University of South Carolina (USC) invites applications for a nine-month, Professional-Track Teaching Assistant Professor position in the Information and Communication Studies Unit, with an anticipated start date of August 16, 2027.
The Bachelor of Arts in Communication program approaches the discipline from a social scientific perspective. Students learn to use scientific reasoning to interpret communication phenomena, design and conduct communication research, communicate effectively in professional settings, and analyze communication processes and their effects on audiences and society. We seek a dedicated teacher and mentor whose training and teaching align with this orientation and who is committed to a career centered on undergraduate instruction. The successful candidate will regularly teach courses such as Applied Interpersonal Communication, Communication in Teams, Conflict and Negotiation, and Communication in Complex Organizations, among others, preparing students for careers in corporate, nonprofit, agency, and public sector settings.
We are interested in candidates whose teaching addresses organizing as a communicative process, meaning how communication creates, sustains, and transforms organizations and the people who work in and around them. Relevant areas include organizational culture and socialization, organizational discourse and sensemaking, leadership, teams and collaboration across hybrid and distributed work, organizational change, crisis and risk communication in organizational settings, corporate social responsibility and stakeholder communication. We are particularly interested in candidates who can connect foundational organizational communication concepts to contemporary organizational challenges, including digital and technology-mediated work, organizational information practices, data-driven decision-making, artificial intelligence, and collaboration across organizational and disciplinary boundaries. Candidates should be prepared to help students understand and critically examine how communication and information shape organizational practices, relationships, and outcomes. Responsibilities
Teach primarily undergraduate courses in the Communication major, as assigned, with occasional graduate-level teaching.
Develop and revise curriculum to support the growth of the Communication major, including courses connecting organizational communication with leadership, organizational change, information practices, and emerging communication technologies.
Use evidence-based and experiential teaching approaches grounded in a social scientific perspective to help students critically examine how communication and information shape organizational practices, relationships, and outcomes.
Support experiential and career-connected learning through partnerships with corporate, nonprofit, agency, public sector, and community organizations, including applied classroom projects, guest speakers, and other opportunities that connect organizational communication theory with professional practice.
Advise and mentor undergraduate students on internships, professional development, and career pathways; supervise independent studies and applied research projects, as appropriate.
Contribute to assessment of the major’s learning outcomes, accreditation activities, and curriculum review.
Contribute service to the unit, college, university, and profession consistent with a teaching-focused appointment.
Required Education and Experience
An earned Ph.D. in communication or a closely related field by the employment start date.
At least one-year of teaching experience in a higher education environment.
Preferred Qualifications
Applied experience that strengthens classroom teaching, such as work in corporate, agency, nonprofit, or public sector organizations
Teaching expertise or knowledge domain depth in one or more of the following: digital and technology-mediated work, organizational information practices, data-driven decision-making, artificial intelligence, or collaboration across organizational and disciplinary boundaries.
Special Instructions to Applicant
All applicants must complete an online application through https://uscjobs.sc.edu/postings/215790. Applications are due by January 3, 2027. The position will remain open until filled.
Applicants must upload the following documents:
Letter of application addressing their interests and qualifications for the position.
Curriculum vitae.
Teaching statement (1-2 pages) explaining pedagogical approach, experience, and methods for connecting theory with practice.
List of three references, including each references name, telephone number, and email address.
Three letters of recommendation signed and on letterhead (only for candidates selected as finalists)should be emailed directly to Rachel Rolli at rachelrolli@sc.edu. While these letters are listed as optional on the application, they are required prior to interviewing. However, letters may be uploaded to USCJobs at the time of initial application.
Inquiries about this posting should be directed to Search Committee co-chair Dr. Delaney Harness at Delaney.harness@sc.edu.
